questions.question: Which statement about const is correct?
options: A const variable cannot be reassigned, but the contents of a const object or array can still change
A const object can never be modified in any way
const variables can be reassigned inside functions
questions.explanation: const prevents reassignment of the variable itself; properties of an object or elements of an array it holds can still be changed.

questions.question: What does [120, 450, 80, 990].filter((p) => p > 100) return?
questions.explanation: filter keeps only the elements for which the callback returns true, so 80 is removed.

questions.question: What happens if JSON.parse is given invalid text?
options: It throws an error, so untrusted input should be wrapped in try/catch
questions.explanation: JSON.parse throws on invalid input, which is why the lesson recommends try/catch for untrusted text.

questions.question: In import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises", what does the node: prefix indicate?
options: The module must be downloaded from npm first
It is a built-in module that ships with Node
The import only works in the REPL
questions.explanation: The node: prefix marks a built-in module, so it is clearly distinguished from packages installed from npm.
